label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: blockers COMPLETE, other edges 2, pool timeouts 155

A.rule: a non-ledger_app session blocked ledger_app sessions in 36 samples; 155 pool acquisition timeouts

report.summary: The 15:28:27 restart cut the pool from 10 to 2 connections and the acquire timeout from 30 s to 250 ms. An idle-in-transaction session then blocked ledger_app sessions, causing 500/503s and slow transfers.

findings.claim: Transfers had a 24.5% server-error ratio (57×500, 107×503) and p95 1.7 s, p99 2.9 s.
findings.reason: Request metrics show many 5xx responses and a long latency tail.

findings.claim: The restart at 15:28:27 reduced pool max from 10 to 2 and connection timeout from 30000 ms to 250 ms.
findings.reason: Runtime config shows the changed settings after the restart.

findings.claim: The tiny pool was exhausted: 155 acquisition timeouts, pending borrowers and active connections up between 15:28:28 and 15:29:48, max acquire wait 256 ms.
findings.reason: Pool metrics show timeouts and saturation in the same period as the config change.

findings.claim: An 'other' session idle in transaction (50113) blocked ledger_app sessions for up to 1.95 s, holding pool connections longer.
findings.reason: Blocker samples show 50111 and 50112 waiting on 50113 from 15:28:29 to 15:29:51.

findings.claim: The outbox and consumer deliveries were healthy. Arrivals dipped in the same period because fewer transfers committed.
findings.reason: All 507 deliveries succeeded at about 71 ms, with 0 failed. Arrivals tracked publications and dropped during the pool-exhaustion period.

limitations: Blocker sampling is every 2 s and pool gauges every 5 s, so brief events may be missed. The owner of session 50113 is not identified.
14 gauge samples were NaN, and the request counters restarted once, so counts span both sides of the restart.
next_checks: Identify the application behind session 50113 and why it stays idle in transaction.
Restore the pool settings (10 connections, 30 s timeout) and re-test the transfers under the same load.

alternatives.reason: All deliveries succeeded at about 71 ms with 0 failed and no backlog growth.
alternatives.hypothesis: Downstream consumer or outbox delivery slowness caused the failures.

alternatives.reason: Both overlap in time. With the 10-connection pool the same blocking might not have exhausted it.
alternatives.hypothesis: The idle-in-transaction blocker alone caused the failures, independent of pool size.

report.summary: A restart at 15:28:27 shrank the DB pool from 10 to 2 with a 250 ms timeout. An idle-in-transaction session then blocked ledger_app sessions, exhausting the pool and causing 500/503 errors and slow transfers.

findings.claim: The restart at 15:28:27 cut poolMaximumSize from 10 to 2 and connection timeout from 30000 ms to 250 ms.
findings.reason: Runtime config shows the changed values starting at the restart inside the window.

findings.claim: The pool was exhausted: 155 acquisition timeouts against a configured max of 2, with pending and active connections above zero from about 15:28:28 to 15:29:48.
findings.reason: Pool metrics show the timeouts and saturation within the window after the config change.

findings.claim: An idle-in-transaction session (50113) blocked ledger_app sessions for up to 1.95 s between 15:28:29 and 15:29:51, so connections stayed held. With only 2 slots and a 250 ms timeout, this became 500/503 failures (24.5% server errors) and p95 1.7 s.
findings.reason: Blocking, pool saturation and the error and latency window coincide. Failures need both the small pool and the lock holder.

findings.claim: Outbox delivery was not the cause: all 507 deliveries succeeded in about 71 ms. Arrival dips mirror the failed transfers.
findings.reason: There were no failed deliveries, and the consumer latency is flat and fast. Publications track arrivals.

limitations: The source of the idle-in-transaction session 50113 is not identified, and blocking is sampled only every 2 s.
Error counts are not split by time relative to the restart, so the before/after rates are not shown directly.
next_checks: Identify the application or session behind PID 50113 and its transaction start time and query.
Split transfer errors and latency before and after 15:28:27, and re-test with poolMaximumSize=10.

alternatives.reason: Deliveries were all successful and about 71 ms, with no errors or retries.
alternatives.hypothesis: Slow downstream consumer or outbox delivery slowed transfers.

alternatives.reason: With the earlier pool of 10 and a 30 s timeout the same blocking might not have exhausted the pool, but there is no pre-change baseline.
alternatives.hypothesis: The blocking session alone caused the failures, without the pool change.
